method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of the three-component structure and the recursive satisfaction clauses, replay of the variable-assignment and existential examples, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison after documented OLFOL-002 and OLFOL-003 projections. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The introductory definition of structures and satisfaction, its extension from variable-free formulas to variable assignments, and the existential quantifier clause.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A structure for the simplified language consists of a nonempty domain, a domain element interpreting a, and a subset interpreting P. General languages have many predicates and constants, predicates of more than one place, and functions.
samples.checks: All three components, their membership/subset conditions and the generalization are retained; OLFOL-002 corrects only the frozen constants/predicates class error.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For variable-free formulas, satisfaction mirrors formula construction: P(a) holds exactly when a's denotation belongs to P's extension, negation reverses satisfaction, and conjunction requires both conjuncts. In the domain {0,1,2} with a=1 and P={1,2}, P(a) and its double negation hold, while its negation and the contradictory conjunction do not.
samples.checks: The recursive clauses, exact structure values, membership calculation and four satisfaction outcomes are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Quantified formulas require a variable assignment s mapping every variable to a domain element. Satisfaction of P(v_0) is then evaluated for a selected value, and total assignments avoid guessing in advance which variables occur.
samples.checks: The quantifier problem, assignment's function type, totality requirement and infinite variable list remain exact; OLFOL-003 restores the actual domain list {0,1,2}.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Satisfaction is relative to M and s. Atomic, negation and conjunction clauses use s, while existential satisfaction holds when some domain element m makes the body true under the assignment obtained by changing only v_i to m. With the all-zero assignment, m=1 or 2 witnesses the existential even though the original value 0 does not satisfy P.
samples.checks: All five clauses, modified-assignment notation, unchanged-variable condition, witness choices and contrast between the modified and original assignments are retained.

source_observations: OLFOL-002 repairs the impossible claim that constants take multiple argument places; the surrounding a/P example and later language definitions confirm predicates are intended.
OLFOL-003 repairs the assignment range from {1,2,3} to the declared domain {0,1,2}; the later all-zero assignment independently confirms 0 must be available and 3 must not.
The target uses चर-मूल्यांकन consistently with decision T204 and preserves the distinction between an assignment's current value and an existentially modified value.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source after the two unit-specific correction projections.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The simplified language omits the full arity and term-evaluation machinery developed later.
चर-मूल्यांकन is a component-supported technical compound and remains expert-reviewable under T204.
